verdict.summary: You can build a user-facing Gmail agent with an External Google OAuth app. If the app uses restricted Gmail scopes, plan for at least six weeks after submission. If your server stores, processes, or transmits restricted Gmail data, it also needs an annual CASA security assessment.
verdict.activeEffort: 2–4 days, mostly security preparation and review materials (estimate)
verdict.waitTime: 6+ weeks for restricted-scope verification; assessment duration is not stated
verdict.mainGate: A CASA assessment is an approved independent security review. It applies when your server stores, processes, or transmits restricted Gmail data.

recommendation.text: Use one External OAuth app with a confidential Web application client. Each customer connects their own Google account. Keep the client secret only on your backend.

sources.quote: Private Clients: These apps, like web server applications, can securely store the client secret because they run on servers you control.
This means the app is used only by people in your Google Workspace or Cloud Identity organization .

scopeTiers.text: Metadata-only triage needs restricted-scope verification. Server-side metadata handling also requires an annual security assessment.

sources.quote: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.metadata View your email message metadata such as labels and headers, but not the email body.
If you store restricted scope data on servers (or transmit), then you must go through a security assessment.

scopeTiers.need: Read message headers and labels without message bodies.

scopeTiers.text: Reading email content needs restricted-scope verification. Server-side content handling requires an annual security assessment.

sources.quote: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly View your email messages and settings.
the system must undergo an annual security assessment from an independent, third-party assessor that is approved by Google.

scopeTiers.need: Search and read the user's message content.

scopeTiers.text: Mailbox changes need restricted-scope verification. Server-side handling requires an annual security assessment.

sources.quote: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify Read, compose, and send emails from your Gmail account. This scope does not allow immediate, permanent deletion
If you store restricted scope data on servers (or transmit), then you must go through a security assessment.

scopeTiers.need: Label, archive, and mark messages read.

scopeTiers.text: Sending email needs sensitive-scope verification. Prefer this narrow scope over draft management where it fits.

sources.quote: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send Send email on your behalf.
Non-sensitive : These scopes provide the smallest scope of authorization and only require basic OAuth App Verification.

scopeTiers.need: Send an email after the user approves it.

essentials.text: Use Authorization Code flow with offline access for background work. Store refresh tokens encrypted and retain an old token when later exchanges omit one. Access-token lifetime comes from expires_in, not a fixed value.

sources.quote: Set the value to offline if your application needs to refresh access tokens when the user is not present at the browser.
Refresh tokens are valid until the user revokes access or the refresh token expires.
The refresh_token is only returned on the first authorization.
The remaining lifetime of the access token in seconds.

essentials.text: Register one controlled HTTPS callback URL. It must match exactly, including case and trailing slash. Use server-side state to return each customer safely.

sources.quote: Note that the http or https scheme, case, and trailing slash (' / ') must all match.
Redirect URIs must use the HTTPS scheme, not plain HTTP. Localhost URIs (including localhost IP address URIs) are exempt from this rule.

essentials.text: Testing supports up to 100 listed test users. Their authorizations, including offline access, expire seven days after consent.

sources.quote: Projects configured with a publishing status of Testing are limited to up to 100 test users listed in the OAuth consent screen.
Authorizations by a test user will expire seven days from the time of consent.

essentials.text: The project limit is 1,200,000 quota units each minute. The user limit is 6,000 units each minute per project. A sent message costs 100 units.

sources.quote: Per minute per project 1,200,000 quota units
When using the Gmail API, there's also a limit of 500 recipients per email message.

essentials.text: Standard Gmail API use has no additional charge. Google does not charge for the security assessment. You pay the independent CASA assessor directly.

sources.quote: All standard use of the Gmail API is available at no additional cost.
Google does not charge the developer any fees for security assessment.

essentials.text: Publish the External app for any Google Account. Unverified sensitive or restricted apps show a warning and have a lifetime limit of 100 new users.

sources.quote: 100 new users in total, after the app presents the unverified app screen

essentials.text: Publish to production, then choose Prepare for Verification. Submit branding, owned-domain pages, exact scopes, justifications, and an end-to-end English demo video.

sources.quote: Apps in development, testing or staging are not applicable for verification.
Provide a video that demonstrates the functionality, the OAuth flow of the app and shows how the scopes are being used.
Do not request access to data based on “future enhancements” that has not been implemented yet in your app

essentials.text: Restricted data on your server requires an annual approved CASA assessment. Encrypt Gmail data and credentials. Add prompt-injection defenses and report suspected unauthorized access to Google.

sources.quote: the system must undergo an annual security assessment from an independent, third-party assessor that is approved by Google.
Protecting against prompt injection techniques
You agree to promptly notify Google at security@google.com of any known or suspected unauthorized access to the systems, networks, accounts, or other locations where Google Data is stored

requests.text: Open this browser URL and validate that the returned state matches RANDOM_STATE.

sources.quote: https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth
Recommended, offline access will give you both an access and refresh token so that your app can refresh the access token without user interaction.

requests.label: Send the user to sign in

requests.text: Exchange the callback authorization code for access and refresh tokens.

sources.quote: https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token

requests.label: Exchange the code for tokens

requests.text: Use the stored refresh token to obtain a new access token.

sources.quote: https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token
Recommended, offline access will give you both an access and refresh token so that your app can refresh the access token without user interaction.

requests.label: Refresh the access token

requests.text: Fetch the connected Gmail user's profile to verify the token works.

sources.quote: GET https://gmail.googleapis.com/gmail/v1/users/{userId}/profile
After obtaining an access token, it should be included in API requests, preferably as an Authorization: Bearer HTTP header.

requests.label: Check the connection

requests.text: Revoke the supplied token and disconnect the user's authorization.

sources.quote: To programmatically revoke a token, your application makes a request to https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke and includes the token as a parameter:

requests.label: Revoke access

steps.title: Create a Cloud project

detail.text: Create or select a Cloud project in Google Auth Platform. This project owns your consent screen and OAuth client.

sources.quote: For your app to access and use Google OAuth APIs, it must have a corresponding Google Cloud project

steps.output: A Google Cloud project for the Gmail integration.

steps.title: Choose External audience

detail.text: Choose External in Audience. Use Internal only when every user belongs to your own Workspace or Cloud Identity organization.

sources.quote: This means the app is used only by people in your Google Workspace or Cloud Identity organization .

steps.output: An External audience setting and developer contact addresses.

steps.title: Enable Gmail API

detail.text: Enable the Gmail API in the selected Cloud project. This permits your OAuth client to call Gmail API methods.

sources.quote: For your app to access and use Google OAuth APIs, it must have a corresponding Google Cloud project

steps.output: Gmail API enabled in the Cloud project.

steps.title: Create a web client

detail.text: Open Clients and create a Web application client. Keep its secret only on servers you control.

sources.quote: To create a client, navigate to the Google Auth Platform Clients page, select or create a project, register the application if required, click CREATE CLIENT, select the application type, complete the required fields, and click CREATE.

steps.output: A Web application client ID and protected client secret.

steps.title: Register the callback URL

detail.text: Add one HTTPS callback URL under the Web client. Match the deployed scheme, case, and trailing slash exactly.

sources.quote: Note that the http or https scheme, case, and trailing slash (' / ') must all match.

steps.output: One exact HTTPS authorized redirect URI.

steps.title: Draft OAuth handler

detail.text: Use server-side state for the connecting user and return path. Verify it before exchanging the authorization code. Redirect away from callback parameters afterward.

sources.quote: Before handling the OAuth 2.0 response on the server, you should confirm that the state received from Google matches the state sent
To avoid this issue, we recommend that the server first handle the request, then redirect to another URL that doesn't include the response parameters.

steps.title: Add test accounts

detail.text: Keep the app in Testing and add development mailbox accounts. Do not rely on this mode for persistent pilots because grants expire after seven days.

sources.quote: Authorizations by a test user will expire seven days from the time of consent.

steps.output: Listed development Google accounts in the Testing audience.

steps.title: Test narrow scopes

detail.text: Start with gmail.metadata or gmail.readonly. Add modify or send only after the matching feature works and users can see its purpose.

sources.quote: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.metadata View your email message metadata such as labels and headers, but not the email body.
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly View your email messages and settings.

steps.output: A tested feature list mapped to Gmail scopes.

steps.title: Prepare review evidence

detail.text: Draft a justification for each implemented scope. Name the visible feature, Gmail methods, data used, and why narrower access fails.

sources.quote: Do not request access to data based on “future enhancements” that has not been implemented yet in your app

steps.output:
Scope justification draft:
“gmail.readonly supports the visible inbox summary feature. The app reads messages selected by the connected user. It does not use Gmail data to train generalized AI models. gmail.modify is requested only when the user asks the app to label, archive, or mark a message read. No scope is requested for future features.”

steps.title: Verify product domains

detail.text: Verify every authorized domain in Search Console. Put a real product homepage and same-domain privacy policy on an owned domain.

sources.quote: The homepage must be hosted on a verified domain you own
You must verify that you own all domains listed in your Authorized domains section of the OAuth consent screen editor.

steps.output: Verified homepage, privacy policy, and authorized domains.

steps.title: Submit verification request

detail.text: Publish to production and select Prepare for Verification. Upload a video showing the English consent screen, grant flow, and every submitted scope in use.

sources.quote: Apps in development, testing or staging are not applicable for verification.
Must show the end-to-end flow of your app including the OAuth grant process

steps.output: A production verification submission with demo video.

steps.title: Complete CASA assessment

detail.text: Respond quickly to Trust and Safety requests. For server-side restricted data, complete the required annual assessment with Google's approved independent assessor. The restricted-scope verification estimate is six weeks; the assessment is additional, and its duration is not stated.

sources.quote: the system must undergo an annual security assessment from an independent, third-party assessor that is approved by Google.
* Please note that these estimates are not guaranteed and will vary based on developer responsiveness

steps.output: OAuth review result and, where applicable, approved annual security assessment.

steps.title: Store tokens securely

detail.text: Encrypt access and refresh tokens in durable server storage. Send access tokens in Authorization headers rather than URL query strings.

sources.quote: Your application should store both tokens in a secure, long-lived location that is accessible between different invocations of your application.
When possible, the HTTP header is preferable, because query strings tend to be visible in server logs.

steps.output: Encrypted durable storage for tokens, tied to each connected user.

steps.title: Restrict AI data use

detail.text: Use Gmail data only for the connected user's visible feature. Do not use it to train or improve generalized AI models.

sources.quote: Transferring, selling, or using user data to create, train, or improve a machine learning or artificial intelligence model beyond that specific user’s personalized model for the appropriate use case or user-facing feature.

steps.output: A production data-use policy and AI controls.

gotchas.text: Do not use https://mail.google.com/ unless immediate permanent deletion is essential. It bypasses the trash.

sources.quote: Request this scope only if your application needs to immediately and permanently delete threads and messages, bypassing the trash.

gotchas.text: Published but unverified sensitive or restricted apps can only acquire 100 new users over their lifetime.

sources.quote: 100 new users in total, after the app presents the unverified app screen

gotchas.text: Never request scopes for planned AI features. Google can reject scopes that are not implemented.

sources.quote: Do not request access to data based on “future enhancements” that has not been implemented yet in your app

gotchas.text: A personalized Gmail summary can be allowed. Training a general model with Gmail data is prohibited.

sources.quote: To be clear : transfers of data for generalized machine-learning (ML) or artificial intelligence (AI) models are prohibited.

Applications that enhance the email experience for productivity purposes (such as applications for customer relationship management, delayed sending of email or mail merge, or providing generative AI summaries)

whenBlocked.text: Reply to the newest OAuth verification or Trust and Safety email. Check spam for every project owner and editor address.

sources.quote: All communications with the OAuth review team will occur over email to the project owners and project editors configured when setting up your project.

whenBlocked.text: For Cloud account, IAM, or service-account problems, contact Google Cloud Support.

sources.quote: please direct them to Google Cloud Support

whenBlocked.text: If an assessment is required, wait for Trust and Safety to coordinate the approved assessor process.

sources.quote: Google does not charge the developer any fees for security assessment.

uncertain: The sources do not state the CASA assessment duration or the assessor's fee amount.
The sources say Gmail billing changes were planned later in 2026. Confirm current quota billing before launch.
